title: Suricatoos — Fleet Command (signed envelope)
description: A command the fleet hub (commandcenter) queues for ONE node and the node PULLS over its outbound mTLS long-poll (GET /fleet/v1/commands, ADR-0011). The node acts only on a command whose Ed25519 signature verifies against the command key pinned at enroll (a key separate from the fleet CA). Signed bytes = the canonical form: the domain line 'suricatoos-fleet-command-v1' then one length-prefixed line 'key=<len>:<value>\n' per field, in this exact order: schema_version, command_id, node_id, tenant, type, issued_by, issued_at, not_after, nonce, payload_sha256 (<len> = byte length in decimal; same framing as control-plane/remediation/canonical.go). payload is compact JSON and payload_sha256 is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the EXACT bytes of the payload value as transmitted (never of a re-serialization). After the signature the node checks the window [issued_at - skew, not_after + skew], node_id == itself, the nonce and the command_id against its persisted store, the tenant against its local registry, its local policy and its local scan scope. The root validates ONE command; $defs also holds the long-poll response, the payload of each type and the shared primitives the other fleet-*.schema.json files reference.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR.0 of a version the node supports (the PATCH never travels); part of the signed canonical form. The hub only delivers a command whose version is in the node's latest announcement

command_id.description: hub-assigned and unique; the {id} of the ack/result routes. The hub NEVER re-signs a command_id: a redelivery is the same envelope byte for byte. The node RECORDS every final decision except the line-3 ones (bad_window, expired: they depend only on the envelope and the clock), and never a deferred one, keyed by the canonical form and indexed by nonce AND command_id: the SAME canonical form already recorded is a redelivery and gets the recorded ack/result again (verification line 2a, even after not_after); a different canonical form under an already-recorded command_id (or nonce) is rejected as replay

node_id.description: the ONE node this command is for; must equal the CN of the node's own fleet certificate (else rejected: wrong_node)

tenant.description: tenant the command acts on; must be known AND enabled on the node (central: TENANTS_FILE registry; standalone/sensor: FLEET_TENANT). Existing objects are addressed only inside that tenant's gvmd partition

not_after.description: expiry; the node requires issued_at < not_after <= issued_at + 24h

nonce.description: 32 CSPRNG bytes in hex, single-use; the node keeps the store entry until min(not_after, issued_at + 24h) + 7 days. Only envelopes past verification line 3 are recorded (bad_window and expired are final but not recorded), so every entry has issued_at <= t + skew and ends before t + skew + 24h + 7 days from when it was recorded (>= not_after + skew)

payload.description: compact JSON; its shape depends on type (see allOf)

signature.description: standard base64 of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature over the canonical form (not part of the canonical), in CANONICAL form only: 88 characters of the standard alphabet ending in '==', the character before the padding with its 4 low bits zero (A, Q, g or w); no whitespace, URL-safe alphabet or unpadded variant

envelope.description: The shape verification line 0 checks BEFORE authentication: the command envelope with type = command_type_any (an authentic type outside the v1 catalog is then 'unsupported' at line 7) and payload = any object (per-type payload validation is line 8). Same members as #/$defs/command; kept for the F2.1 parity tests.

poll_response.description: 200 body of GET /fleet/v1/commands?wait=N: 1..10 commands for the polling node, oldest issued_at first. Nothing pending → 204 with no body.

no_control.description: Rejects ASCII control characters (incl. CR/LF) and the noncharacters U+FFFE/U+FFFF, which XML 1.0 forbids: no log/XML/line injection, nothing gvmd's XML cannot carry, and no trailing newline slipping past a '$' anchor in validators where '$' also matches before a final newline. (An unpaired surrogate is refused by the JSON parser rules, not here.)

uuid.description: lowercase canonical UUID (also the shape of every gvmd object id)

node_id.description: fleet node identity = CN of the node certificate issued by the FLEET CA (OU=fleet-node)

tenant.description: a tenant name LOCAL to the node (its TENANTS_FILE or FLEET_TENANT): two nodes may both have 'acme'. The hub keys tenants, and its RBAC, by (node_id, tenant)

issued_by.description: PSEUDONYMOUS id of the hub operator who issued the command (non-repudiation; recorded in the node's local audit); the hub keeps the mapping to the person. No '@' and no space: an e-mail is refused by construction (LGPD minimization)

utc_time.description: RFC 3339, UTC, whole seconds, 'Z' suffix — byte-identical to the canonical rendering (no fraction, no offset) — and a REAL calendar instant: the pattern pins the field ranges (no hour 24, no second 60), format date-time the calendar (no Feb 30)

pin.description: 'sha256:' + hex SHA-256 of a DER structure (same format as the control-plane CA Fingerprint)

gvm_comment.description: gvmd object comment; the node prefixes 'fleet:<command_id> ' for traceability in the GSA

gmp_filter.description: EXPLICIT GMP filter string applied inside the addressed report only; the node never falls back to gvmd's implicit or saved filters (ADR-0011 D1)

ip_literal.description: IPv4/IPv6 literal; the node parses it authoritatively (a hostname is refused)

ip_or_cidr.description: IPv4/IPv6 or CIDR LITERAL — never a hostname (no scan-time DNS rebinding). The node re-checks it with its local scope gate (a CIDR containing a self/hub IP is denied)

port_range.description: GVM port_range, same grammar scan_bridge.py accepts, e.g. T:1-65535

alive_test.description: Contract NAME of a set of gvmd alive-test methods (ADR-0011 table); fleet_ops never sends this name to gvmd. gvmd 26 refuses a combined literal as one alive_tests value, so the node sends each method of the set as one <alive_test> sub-element of <alive_tests>, built with python-gvm's XmlCommand: 'ICMP, TCP-SYN Service & ARP Ping' = ICMP Ping + TCP-SYN Service Ping + ARP Ping (the default when omitted); 'ICMP, TCP-ACK Service & ARP Ping' = ICMP Ping + TCP-ACK Service Ping + ARP Ping (the fallback, ONLY if gvmd refuses the default); 'ICMP & TCP-ACK Service Ping', 'ICMP & ARP Ping' and 'TCP-ACK Service & ARP Ping' = their two methods; any other value = one sub-element, itself. alive_test_effective reports the set actually applied, by name. Never a silent fall back to 'Consider Alive' or 'Scan Config Default'. That gvmd 26.x accepts the default this way is a LAB confirmation item (F2.3).

agent_id.description: endpoint agent id = CN of the agent's scanner certificate (same charset rule as control-plane/enroll validateAgentID). By default the agent uses the host's HOSTNAME as agent_id, so it MAY be personal data (e.g. a person's name in the machine name): prefer non-personal ids at agent enroll

token_id.description: public id of a scanner bootstrap token (st_<id>.<secret>, ADR-0004) — never the secret

schema_version_wire.description: Wire form of schema_version: MAJOR.MINOR.0 with MAJOR and MINOR in decimal WITHOUT leading zeros (01.0.0 and 1.00.0 are out; the PATCH never travels). VERSION-INVARIANT: its name, being a TOP-LEVEL member of every versioned body (all but the 426 body) and envelope (its position among the members is irrelevant: JSON objects are unordered), and this shape never change, not even in a new MAJOR. The receiver reads it before full validation: missing at the top level, not a string or outside this pattern => 400; inside it but a version the hub does not support => 426 with fleet-heartbeat.schema.json#/$defs/version_unsupported. Each body pins its contract version with const (v1: 1.0.0)

schema_versions.description: MAJOR.MINOR contract versions the sender supports. The PATCH is editorial only and never travels: every body and envelope carries schema_version = MAJOR.MINOR.0. Each side speaks the highest version common to the other side's latest announcement (node: enroll, renew, every heartbeat; hub: their responses and the 426 body). Version-invariant member: its shape never changes, not even in a new MAJOR

command_type_any.description: a command type AS RECEIVED (used where a rejection must echo a type outside the v1 catalog, reason=unsupported); v1 values are command_type

report_format.description: symbolic export format; the node maps (format, lang) to a local report_format id

report_variant.description: report EDITION (plan decision D10): technical = today's Suricatoos Premium PDF; client = no false positives, Log only as a count, low QoD shown as 'to validate'; executive = summary. Each (edition, language) is its own report-format object (slice R5); gvm-* formats only exist as technical. Full vs delta is NOT a variant (see delta_report_id)

iana_timezone.description: IANA tz name, e.g. America/Sao_Paulo or UTC

icalendar.description: RFC 5545 VCALENDAR text (TAB, CR and LF allowed; no other C0 control, no U+FFFE/U+FFFF: only XML 1.0 characters) as gvmd's create_schedule expects

payload_task_ref.description: task.start | task.stop | task.resume | task.delete (delete = trash, never ultimate). For start/resume the node re-checks the hosts of the task's target against the tenant scope before deciding (scope_denied; a non-literal host is refused)

target_id.description: must be owned by the tenant's gvmd user; its hosts are re-checked against the tenant scope (scope_denied; a non-literal host is refused)

schedule_id.description: links the new task to an existing schedule owned by the tenant
a schedule owned by the tenant links it, and then the hosts of the task's target are re-checked against the tenant scope (scope_denied); "" unlinks

payload_task_clone.description: task.clone. When the source task has a schedule (the clone would run on it), the hosts of its target are re-checked against the tenant scope first (scope_denied; a non-literal host is refused).

name.description: name of the clone (default: gvmd's 'Clone of ...')

payload_target_create.description: Scope-gated: every hosts entry must be an IP/CIDR literal inside the tenant's LOCAL scope and outside the absolute deny list (loopback, link-local/metadata, multicast, unspecified, and the node's own and the hub's IPs — a CIDR that CONTAINS one of those is denied too, and exclude_hosts never rescues it; the connector adds the hub's IPs itself: resolved from FLEET_HUB_URL at start-up and on every connection, plus each connection's remote IP). exclude_hosts entries only need to be literals (excluding never widens). No credentials, no asset filter, no reverse lookup (out of v1 by design). Exactly one of port_list_id | port_range.

payload_target_modify.description: The RESULTING hosts pass the same scope gate as target.create on every target.modify: the new ones, or the current ones read from gvmd when hosts is absent. So shrinking exclude_hosts only widens the target inside the checked scope (exclude_hosts: literals only, never a rescue for a CIDR that contains a self/hub IP). Ports change ONLY through port_list_id: gvmd's modify_target has no port_range.

payload_schedule_create.description: Creates a schedule and, when task_ids is present, links each task to it (each link is a task modification: the node's local policy must also allow task.modify). The hosts of those tasks' targets are re-checked against the tenant scope first (scope_denied; a non-literal host is refused).

payload_schedule_modify.description: Modifies a schedule. The hosts of the targets of every task linked to it are re-checked against the tenant scope first (scope_denied; a non-literal host is refused).

payload_report_export.description: Detailed findings leave the node ONLY through this explicit command, as one gzip artifact (PUT /fleet/v1/artifacts/{command_id}/{name}). Every input is explicit: format, lang, variant (the report EDITION — technical | client | executive) and the GMP filter. gvm-* formats only exist as lang 'en' + variant 'technical'. Full vs delta is expressed ONLY by the optional delta_report_id: present = delta against that older report of the SAME task, absent = full. A schema-valid (format, lang, variant) the node does not advertise in its state capabilities.report_formats is rejected at runtime with reason unsupported_report_variant (until slice R5 ships, nodes advertise only technical).

delta_report_id.description: optional: older report of the SAME task to diff against; present = delta export, absent = full export (independent of variant)

payload_report_summary.description: Counts of ONE report (D4). There is NO free filter: the node builds the explicit GMP filter from these fixed parameters ('apply_overrides=<0|1> min_qod=<n> levels=<levels> rows=-1'), so narrowing by host, port, NVT, name, CVE or vulnerability is impossible by construction. Counts in the local sensitive budget.

levels.description: non-empty subset of c (critical), h, m, l, g (log), each at most once, in this order

payload_agent_ref.description: agent.scan_now: re-runs the agent's LOCAL inventory collection now (ADR-0001 passive agent) — not a network scan

payload_agent_revoke.description: Revokes ONLY this agent's scanner certificate serial(s); irreversible (the agent must re-enroll).

reason.description: free text recorded in the node's local audit

payload_enroll_token_create.description: Mints a scanner bootstrap token (ADR-0004) for the envelope's tenant, for ENDPOINT AGENTS only (v1): scanner-sensor tokens stay a local, admin-bearer action (ADR-0007: whoever sets Scope.Tenant controls tenant -> cert O -> partition). The secret is returned ONCE in the result (contains_secret=true). Caps tighter than the admin API: ttl <= 168h, deployment max_uses <= 1000.

policy.description: cert OU the enrolled agent receives; v1 accepts only agent-endpoint

payload_enroll_token_revoke.description: Revokes ONLY the token: future enrollments with it stop. Certificates already issued with it stay valid — revoking them in bulk is a LOCAL action (today's DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id} revokes everything; slice F2.2 adds a token-only route for the connector).

payload_sensor_job_enqueue.description: Enqueues an ADR-0007 sensor scan job (source=operator-scope) for the envelope's tenant. ALL targets must pass the node's scope gate — one out-of-scope target rejects the whole command (scope_denied); nothing is dropped silently. v1 carries only targets and ports (which the sensor honors): the sensor applies ITS OWN alive test, scan config and maximum duration (ADR-0007 scanrun), so the contract does not pretend to set them.
